verses.text: There was a man named Elkanah from Ramathaim Zophim in Ephraim's hill country. He was an Ephraimite, the son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph.
He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
Every year Elkanah left his town to worship and offer sacrifices to the LORD of Armies at Shiloh. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served there as priests to the LORD.
On the day Elkanah offered his sacrifice, he gave portions to Peninnah and all her sons and daughters.
He gave Hannah a double portion because he loved her, though the LORD had kept her from having children.
Her rival tormented her to upset her because the LORD had kept her from having children.
This went on year after year whenever Hannah went up to the LORD's house. Peninnah would taunt her until Hannah cried and wouldn't eat.
Her husband Elkanah asked her, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why are you grieving? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
After they finished eating and drinking at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Eli the priest was sitting in his seat by the doorpost of the LORD's temple.
Hannah was in deep anguish. She prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

She made a vow: “LORD of Armies, if you look at your servant's suffering, remember me and don't forget me, and give me a son, I'll give him to you for his whole life. No razor will ever touch his head.”
As she kept praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
Hannah was praying in her heart. Her lips moved, but her voice couldn't be heard. Eli thought she was drunk.
He asked her, “How long are you going to stay drunk? Put the wine away.”
Hannah answered, “No, sir. I'm a woman in deep distress. I haven't had any wine or strong drink. I've been pouring out my heart before the LORD.
Please don't think I'm a wicked woman. I've been speaking out of all my pain and grief.”
Eli answered, “Go in peace. May the God of Israel give you what you've asked him for.”
She said, “May I find favor with you.” Then she went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.
They got up early the next morning and worshiped the LORD. Then they went back home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.
In time Hannah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “I asked the LORD for him.”
Elkanah and his whole household went up to bring the yearly sacrifice to the LORD and fulfill his vow.
Hannah stayed behind. She told her husband, “Once the boy is weaned, I'll take him to appear before the LORD and stay there for good.”
Elkanah told her, “Do what seems best to you. Stay here until you've weaned him. May the LORD make his word stand.” So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until he was weaned.
When she'd weaned him, she took him to the LORD's house at Shiloh, bringing three bulls, an ephah of flour, and a container of wine. The boy was still young.
They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
Hannah said, “Pardon me, sir. As surely as you live, I'm the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
I prayed for this child, and the LORD gave me what I asked him for.
Now I'm giving him to the LORD. He belongs to the LORD for as long as he lives.” And he worshiped the LORD there.
